Team — paste below is the draft material I recommend we send to Oliver. Please review inline comments by EOD 6/13. I attached a mapping workbook for your review (governance_mapping.xlsx).

=== Draft reply to customer (technical summary) ===
1) EU AI Act classification and position - For the described use (claims routing + agent Q&A), Redwood's assessment: classification can be context-dependent. If the model is used to make automated decisions that have legal or significant effects (e.g., automated claim denials, premium adjustments), the system would fall under "high-risk". However, when used as an assistive tool for human agents with human-in-the-loop review and no automated adverse action, the default classification for a vendor-provided inference API is typically NOT automatically "high-risk".
- Proposed mitigations we will document: required human oversight UI patterns, decision-logging and justification metadata (per-request provenance), stricter data minimization for EU workloads, model version pinning and rollout gates, and attested evaluation samples for fairness and safety.

2) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary) - We map NIST functions to Redwood artifacts:
  - Govern: model onboarding checklist, risk tiering doc, third-party attestations (SOC2, pen-test summaries)
  - Map: data inventory, training data provenance summary (where available), vendor model card and known limitations
  - Measure: continuous evaluation harness (metric dashboards for fidelity, hallucination rate, latency and per-route token cost)
  - Manage: release rollouts (canary/A-B), automated rollback on regression gates, KV/prefix cache isolation per-tenant
  - Use: SLA, access control, and operator runbooks

Evidence we can provide: NIST_EUAct_Mapping_20260614.docx, governance_mapping.xlsx, sample eval reports (anonymized), SOC2 Type II summary, and runtime logs for an agreed timebox.

3) Regression / eval approach (operational detail)
- Baseline: curated prompt/eval corpus per-customer (we request an initial seed of 200–500 prompts from Granite for targeted scenarios).
- Metrics: per-prompt label accuracy (for structured outputs), factuality score (model hallucination flagging), response stability (token-level divergence after updates), latency, and a small human-rated quality signal (N=50 samples per release).
- Automation: daily automated regression runs against the baseline with threshold-based gates (fail build if regression > X% on critical metrics), weekly sampling and human review of outliers, and monthly full-sweep comparative evals when model or quantization changes occur.
- Rollout: staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automatic rollback trigger on metric degradation and an on-call escalation runbook.

Attachments: governance_mapping.xlsx (xlsx)

Ben
Senior Architect, Product Reliability — Redwood Inference

Oliver — thanks, we compiled the requested materials and an appendix that addresses EU residency and the roadmap items you flagged. Summary (attachments + commitments below). Full evidence is attached as a single archive for download: Granite_Redwood_Evidence_Package_20260614.zip (zip).

Quick summary highlights:
- EU Act classification: Based on your current human-in-the-loop topology, Redwood recommends classifying the integration as a non-automated decision support system (not automatically "high-risk") but we document the controls required if you move to automated routing/denial usecases. See the NIST_EUAct_Mapping_20260614.docx for the control trace and the policy wording we recommend for contract addenda.
- NIST AI RMF: Provided a mapped artifact set and evidence pointers (Govern/Map/Measure/Manage/Use). We included an anonymized regression report from a recent release showing the automated daily-run baseline and human review flags. Metrics in the sample: factuality/hallucination rate (automated classifier + human adjudication), per-prompt correctness, latency percentiles, and token-cost deltas.
- Regression / Eval approach we will supply to Granite:
  - Seed corpus: we ask Granite to provide 300 representative prompts/queries (we can help curate).
  - Automated daily runs against the corpus with threshold-based gates (we propose a critical-metric gate of >4% relative regression on correctness or >8% on hallucination triggers a block).
  - Human review of flagged regressions within 48 hours. Monthly full-sweep comparative evals for model and quantization updates.
  - Rollout: 1% canary -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback and immediate notification to your security/Platform teams if gates fail.
- EU residency & routing: Yes — Redwood offers EU-region-only inference pools for regulated workloads. We can route requests for EU accounts to EU-only clusters and supply region-limited audit logs and KMS integration for key residency. This is available as a configuration on Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted accounts we can enable EU-only tenancy with contractual commitments.
